[Project overview]{.eyebrow}

::: {.lead}
We build education and outreach activities that put real sequencing data in
students' hands.
:::

Recognizing a gap in the genomics curriculum, we developed a course on the human
microbiome in which students generate and analyze next-generation sequencing
data. We helped craft a game on host-parasite coevolution called the Red Queen's
Race, an innovative approach to curriculum development. We integrated outreach
into the classroom, where students write for a course blog on peer-reviewed
literature.

As a Chancellor's Innovation in Technology and E-learning (CITE) fellow at UAF,
we developed further teaching innovations for undergraduate education, including
integrating the Learning Glass into flipped classroom activities and online
learning.

Building on our nanopore expertise, we have run multiple workshops exploring
genomics with the MinION platform. We developed a mobile laboratory for
genomics, and in 2018 and 2019 the lab led workshops with STEMSEAS aboard the
R/V *Sikuliaq*, a 261-foot oceanographic research ship. In 2020 the lab ran a
workshop engaging undergraduates in the search for novel antibiotics in soil
microbes.
